subject: Logic
title: Likelihood Ratios
description: A quick, practical guide to Likelihood Ratios.

hook.text: Two suspects. Same evidence. Who does it point to more? The likelihood ratio tells you.

buildup.text: A likelihood ratio compares how probable the evidence is under two competing hypotheses.

discovery.text: If the evidence is 10× more likely under hypothesis A than B, A gets a strong evidential boost.

twist.text: A ratio of 1 means the evidence is equally likely under both. It's useless for deciding.

climax.text: Likelihood ratios let you weigh evidence without getting lost in raw probability numbers.

punchline.text: How much more likely under A than B?

quiz.question: What does a likelihood ratio of 1 mean?
